subject: Immediate: PioneerLedger spike in latency & errors — CEO notified, mitigation underway
messages:
From: Emma Ross <emma.ross@pioneerledger.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: latency spikes & 503s since last night (prod)

Kimberly —

We started seeing elevated tail latency and intermittent 503 errors on our production inference routes (pioneer-transaction-v2) late last night (around 23:40 UTC). Traffic is within normal bounds for our committed reserved throughput, but latency has spiked from 120ms p95 to ~1.8s and error rate has climbed to ~2.5% (5xx). This is impacting customer-facing flows during our morning window.

I've attached the logs we captured and a short gif of the frontend impact. We need immediate mitigation: either routing to a healthy fallback, temporary capacity bump, or an emergency failover plan. Our CTO is on standby; please escalate to your execs if required.

What we need right now:
- Short-term routing/fallback so our live sessions do not drop
- Expected ETA for a hotfix or capacity change
- Confirmation of whether this is a reserved-capacity shortfall or an infra degradation

Thanks — this is high priority.

Emma Ross
Head of Platform, PioneerLedger
emma.ross@pioneerledger.com
Attachments: pioneer_latency_logs_20280606-20280607.zip
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@pioneerledger.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: latency spikes & 503s since last night (prod)

Emma — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately. Preliminary triage: we are seeing sustained queueing on the PioneerLedger dedicated GPU pool and an unexpected burst from a new batch job that started rolling at 22:50 UTC. That job looks to be using a larger context length variant and it's increasing per-request GPU time.

Immediate actions we are taking (next 2 hours):
- Route new inference requests for pioneer-transaction-v2 to the configured fallback model variant with lower context costs (non-disruptive routing rule, should preserve correctness for most requests).
- Temporarily throttle non-essential background jobs in the same pool (ops running now).
- Stand up a short-lived spare node group and attach to PioneerLedger's pool (SRE on it now).
- We will open a dedicated bridge and include execs if we cannot bring p95 back under 300ms in 90 minutes.

I have looped in Naomi (SRE lead), Marcus (Capacity & Product), and Rishi (VP Eng) for visibility and next steps. I'll post updates in this thread.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: quick technical triage findings for PioneerLedger saturation

Internal note — do not forward externally yet.

Summary of findings (from logs + metrics):
- Root cause: Dedicated pool saturation caused by an unaccounted batch job that began at 22:50 UTC 2028-06-06. That job increases mean tokens-per-request by ~4x for that variant; combined with normal peak traffic created sustained queuing.
- Our autoscaler did not spin additional reserved nodes because the job flagged as burst/ephemeral under the wrong priority class — needs fix.
- We also observed inefficient batching for that variant (batch window set too large), which amplifies GPU work per batch.

Short-term remediation (in progress):
1) Force-route live production traffic to fallback variant (Kimberly's team initiated) — should lower p95 immediately.
2) SRE to create a 6-node hot pool (spare-dedicated) attached just for PioneerLedger; expect attachment completed by 2028-06-08T11:00Z.
3) Capacity: Marcus to authorize immediate quota expansion from reserved 80k toks/s to 120k toks/s for 48 hours to cover peak and run post-mortem.
4) Ops: throttle/disable the non-critical batch job in customer namespace; schedule for re-run in off-peak after optimization.

Longer-term: change priority classification rules for ephemeral jobs, tighten batching heuristics for models with long context, and add a policy to proactively add hot nodes when p95 > 400ms for >5m.

Action items assigned:
- Marcus: confirm temporary quota increase + cost estimate (ETA 2 hours)
- Rishi: confirm exec notification and sign-off for credits if appropriate
- Grace: prepare customer-facing timeline and credit proposal
- Naomi: finish post-incident collection and RFC for autoscaler priority bug

Naomi Feldman
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@pioneerledger.com>, procurement@pioneerledger.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: PioneerLedger spike in latency & errors — CEO notified, mitigation underway

Emma — brief update and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption. We hit dedicated-pool saturation driven by an unexpected high-cost batch job. The good news: the emergency routing to the fallback variant reduced p95 to ~260ms within 20 minutes and error rate returned to baseline.

What we've done and when:
- 2028-06-07 10:10 UTC: emergency routing to fallback model variant (reduced per-request GPU time).
- 2028-06-08 11:00 UTC: attached a 6-node hot pool to PioneerLedger reserved capacity (temporary increase to 120k toks/s).
- 2028-06-08 12:30 UTC: throttled non-essential batch job and scheduled optimized re-run for off-peak.

Planned permanence and customer support:
- We propose a permanent reserved uplift to 110k toks/s and a focused optimization of your heavy batch job (payload/context reduction). Marcus will share a cost & timeline estimate by EOD.
- As a gesture for the production impact, Rishi has pre-approved a one-time service credit equivalent to 5% of last month's invoice; Grace will share the credit details.
- We will run a joint technical review next week (calendar invite attached) and produce a short post-mortem + action RFC within 5 business days.

Attachments: redwood_mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf

Please confirm you received this and whether the proposed permanent uplift and review timeline are acceptable. If you want I can loop our COO/CEO into the conversation; Rishi is copied for exec visibility.

Thanks — we will keep the bridge open until you confirm stabilization for your next two peak cycles.

—Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
